rv.q: What we do get is a slick, smart, superbly paced show courtesy of staging and creative director Ash Jacks McCready, featuring a pounding score by composer Evan Duffy, banks of in-yer-face spotlights from lighting designer Hugo Mercier Bosseny and, most importantly, tremendous tricks.
At best, the magic on display here is jaw-dropping.
It could scarcely be more pompous – but happily, there are plenty of entertaining tricks to keep pomp-phobes like myself onside.
The big-bang, big-prop illusions are undeniably impressive — he’s here! No, that’s impossible, he’s there! — without quite raising the heart rate like they might.
Whether you're a fan of magic or just looking for an entertaining, family-friendly show, Now You See Me Live is well worth seeing.
It is in moments like this that Now You See Me Live truly excels.
This production understands that how a thing is lit is part of how a thing is done.
It’s fun, flashy, and has magical moments.
So, it’s good family fun, but the team should be aware that not every adult in the show is heterosexual.
Those brand new to magic or who have expectations somewhere around the level of the Mariana Trench will probably have a fine time but there are better alternatives around London.
It is an incredible blend of illusion, theatre, storytelling, comedy and spectacle that keeps you completely engaged from start to finish.
Now You See Me Live is a high-octane, jaw-dropping spectacle that will have you questioning if anything you’re seeing is what it seems.
It's a slick, fun and thoroughly entertaining night out, it delivers exactly what it promises.
A bombardment of spectacular illusion, intelligent sleight of hand and mammoth visuals that combine to create an unforgettable evening of magic.

Aimed at audiences aged five and above, Now You See Me makes for a thoroughly enjoyable family outing, while delivering enough skill, spectacle and showmanship to keep adult audiences equally entertained.
Albeit amusing and generally well put together, this compilation of conventional illusions isn't a strong enough rival to other similar shows currently on offer across the London scene.
That said, there is still plenty to enjoy here, making the show far from the disaster it ought to be.
It’s hard to believe what you’ve seen in Now You See Me Live – and not in a good way.

The illusions were magical, the tricks made you shake your head in wonderment, the non-stop action had you looking up, down, in the shadows, in the private boxes, and in the aisles, because the action was not just happening on the stage.
This slick mix of illusion, mind games and cutting edge tech lands with a real wow factor.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this magic spectacular: some praise the jaw-dropping illusions and slick production, while others find it loud, unoriginal, and only loosely connected to the film franchise that inspired it.
